title: Boss: the Black Friday cache review
summary: A cache dashboard snapshot from a bad morning. Size the cache, read the counters, find the hot key and write the review tool the on-call team will run next time.

steps.title: The ticket
body: **INC-2291: feed and product pages slow, 09:00-09:40.** You are asked to review the cache before the next
sale. The on-call engineer attached this snapshot:
cache cluster  shop-cache (6 nodes, maxmemory 12gb each, maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru)
app config:   TTL 300 s (no jitter), no request coalescing
Four tasks, each a small tool. Together they are the review you would attach to the postmortem: is the
cache big enough, what is its real hit ratio, which key is hot, and what must change before the sale.

steps.title: How much memory for the hot set?
prompt: Write `long CacheBytes(long keys, int keyBytes, int valueBytes, int overheadBytes, double headroom)`:
- the bytes `keys` entries take: `keys × (keyBytes + valueBytes + overheadBytes)`;
- then leave `headroom` free (`0.25` means the data may fill only 75 % of memory): divide by
`1 − headroom` and round **up** to a whole byte.
- `headroom` must be at least `0` and below `1`, otherwise throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
2 million hot products with 20-byte keys, 2,000-byte values and 64 bytes of overhead, with 25 % headroom,
need `5,557,333,334` bytes (about 5.2 GiB).
starter: long CacheBytes(long keys, int keyBytes, int valueBytes, int overheadBytes, double headroom)
solution: long CacheBytes(long keys, int keyBytes, int valueBytes, int overheadBytes, double headroom)
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("2 million products with 25 % headroom", 5557333334L, CacheBytes(2_000_000, 20, 2000, 64, 0.25));
Dojo.Eq("no headroom is just the data", 4168000000L, CacheBytes(2_000_000, 20, 2000, 64, 0));
Dojo.Eq("large key counts do not overflow", 1_000_000_000_000L, CacheBytes(10_000_000_000L, 20, 60, 20, 0));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("headroom of 1 is rejected", () => CacheBytes(1, 1, 1, 1, 1));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("negative headroom is rejected", () => CacheBytes(1, 1, 1, 1, -0.1));
steps.explain: Six 12 GB nodes is 72 GB: the hot set fits easily, so memory is not why cache-1 is on fire. Sizing first stops you buying the wrong fix.

steps.title: The real hit ratio
prompt: Write `double HitRatioBetween(string before, string after)`. Each argument is the text of `INFO stats`:
lines of `name:value` (lines may end in `\r\n`, and other lines such as `# Stats` appear too).
Return the hit ratio **between** the two snapshots: the change in `keyspace_hits` divided by the change in
`keyspace_hits` plus `keyspace_misses`. Return `0` when there were no lookups in between. If a field is
missing, throw `FormatException`.
You may write helper functions.
template: {{CODE}}

var dojoBefore = "# Stats
total_connections_received:9001
keyspace_hits:812004110
keyspace_misses:90012000
evicted_keys:4100220
";

var dojoAfter = "# Stats
total_connections_received:9050
keyspace_hits:812151110
keyspace_misses:90117000
evicted_keys:4201220
";
Dojo.Eq("the minute's hit ratio, not the lifetime one", 0.583, Math.Round(HitRatioBetween(dojoBefore, dojoAfter), 3));
Dojo.Eq("works with plain \\n line ends", 0.75, HitRatioBetween("keyspace_hits:10\nkeyspace_misses:10", "keyspace_hits:40\nkeyspace_misses:20"));
Dojo.Eq("no lookups in between gives 0", 0.0, HitRatioBetween(dojoBefore, dojoBefore));
Dojo.Throws<FormatException>("a missing field is an error", () => HitRatioBetween("keyspace_hits:1", "keyspace_hits:2"));

steps.title: Which key is hot?
prompt: The on-call engineer sampled 100 commands on `cache-1` (the keys only). Write
`List<(string Key, double Share)> TopKeys(string[] sample, int n)`:
- count each key in the sample;
- return the `n` most frequent, most frequent first, ties broken by key in **ordinal** order;
- `Share` is the key's count divided by the sample size;
- an empty sample gives an empty list; fewer than `n` distinct keys gives them all.
starter: List<(string Key, double Share)> TopKeys(string[] sample, int n)
solution: List<(string Key, double Share)> TopKeys(string[] sample, int n)
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoSample = Enumerable.Repeat("feed:user:9001", 50)
.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat("feed:user:2210", 8))
.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat("feed:user:17", 8))
.Concat(Enumerable.Range(100, 34).Select(i => $"feed:user:{i}"))
.ToArray();
var dojoTop = TopKeys(dojoSample, 3);
Dojo.Eq("the top three keys, ties in ordinal order", new List<string> { "feed:user:9001", "feed:user:17", "feed:user:2210" }, dojoTop.Select(x => x.Key).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("their shares of the sample", new List<double> { 0.5, 0.08, 0.08 }, dojoTop.Select(x => Math.Round(x.Share, 3)).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("asking for more than exist returns them all", 37, TopKeys(dojoSample, 100).Count);
Dojo.Eq("an empty sample gives nothing", 0, TopKeys(new string[0], 3).Count);
steps.explain: Half of one node's traffic is one key. That is why cache-1 runs at 96,400 ops/s and the others at 20,000: a near cache for keys like this, not more nodes.

steps.title: The review tool
prompt: Write `List<string> Review(CacheSnapshot s)`. The record (already defined by the tests) is:
```csharp
record CacheSnapshot(string Policy, double HitRatio, long EvictionsPerSec,
double MaxNodeCpu, double MedianNodeCpu, bool TtlJitter, bool Coalescing);
Return these findings, in this order, for each rule that applies (exact text):
1. `Policy` is `"noeviction"`: `"noeviction on a pure cache: use allkeys-lfu"`
2. `EvictionsPerSec > 0` and `HitRatio < 0.9`: `"too small: evicting while the hit ratio is under 90%"`
3. `MaxNodeCpu >= 80` and `MaxNodeCpu >= 3 × MedianNodeCpu`: `"hot key: one node is much busier than the rest"`
4. no TTL jitter: `"no TTL jitter"`
5. no coalescing: `"no request coalescing"`
A healthy cache gives an empty list.
solution: if (s.Policy == "noeviction") findings.Add("noeviction on a pure cache: use allkeys-lfu");
if (s.EvictionsPerSec > 0 && s.HitRatio < 0.9) findings.Add("too small: evicting while the hit ratio is under 90%");
if (s.MaxNodeCpu >= 80 && s.MaxNodeCpu >= 3 * s.MedianNodeCpu) findings.Add("hot key: one node is much busier than the rest");
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoIncident = Review(new CacheSnapshot("allkeys-lru", 0.58, 1700, 100, 20, false, false));

Dojo.Eq("the 09:00 snapshot", new List<string> { "too small: evicting while the hit ratio is under 90%", "hot key: one node is much busier than the rest", "no TTL jitter", "no request coalescing" }, dojoIncident);
Dojo.Eq("a healthy cache has no findings", new List<string>(), Review(new CacheSnapshot("allkeys-lfu", 0.97, 0, 35, 30, true, true)));
Dojo.Eq("noeviction is flagged", new List<string> { "noeviction on a pure cache: use allkeys-lfu" }, Review(new CacheSnapshot("noeviction", 0.95, 0, 50, 45, true, true)));
Dojo.Eq("evicting at a 95 % hit ratio is fine", new List<string>(), Review(new CacheSnapshot("allkeys-lfu", 0.95, 300, 40, 35, true, true)));
Dojo.Eq("80 % against a 30 % median is not 3x", new List<string>(), Review(new CacheSnapshot("allkeys-lfu", 0.95, 0, 80, 30, true, true)));
Dojo.Eq("90 % against a 30 % median is a hot key", new List<string> { "hot key: one node is much busier than the rest" }, Review(new CacheSnapshot("allkeys-lfu", 0.95, 0, 90, 30, true, true)));
record CacheSnapshot(string Policy, double HitRatio, long EvictionsPerSec, double MaxNodeCpu, double MedianNodeCpu, bool TtlJitter, bool Coalescing);
explain: The review for INC-2291: the hit ratio dropped because the cache was evicting (worth checking after the hot
key is fixed, since retries and duplicate fills inflate misses too), one celebrity key pinned cache-1, and
synchronised TTLs plus no coalescing turned each expiry into a stampede on a database already at 97 %.
